publication_context: Independent follow-up to Hashimoto and Ohgushi 2023 Ecology and Evolution DOI 10.1002/ece3.10164
randomization_unit: WHOLE independent cage containing all host plants

primary.label: Does randomized edible food support modify the TOTAL effect of adding Sericinus?
primary.response: flight-capable A adults / all originally assigned focal A larvae; block-equal cage risk contrasts
primary.interpretation: Assigned food-support strategy x total invader addition, NOT biomass-only mediator or direct interaction

key_secondary.label: Does food support modify the contrast between equal-headcount added S and A?
key_secondary.interpretation: Extra species assignment bundled with different species-specific consumption; NOT identified direct interference

outcomes.diapause_alive: unknown eventual adult emergence, not death
outcomes.pupa_alive_pending_emergence: unknown eventual adult emergence, not death

negative_controls: True experiment lacks prior source-catapult of 2012 mixed-cage endpoints to new treatments
Postrandomization observed edible leaf area never determines inclusion
Focal native A larvae never pooled with added A
Additional A and S headcount parity does not mean equal food consumption
Plant-quality and contact-pathway mediation remain unidentified from support strategy alone
